title: Battle modes
docText: Scenario mode (Epic tab) and generic mode (Battle tab). PvP and PvC, each up to 5 players.
codeBehaviour: Lobby allows 2–5 total players (humans or 1 human + CPUs). Scenario mode is a setup flag; nothing branches on it.
notes: Scenario mode has no distinct behaviour in the engine.

title: All-era / single-era
docText: Single era games use only that era's locations and Great People and open on the era's first birth. All era games draw from all of history and open on a start era (random unless chosen).
codeBehaviour: openingDeal: single era opens on eraStartYear(singleEra) with gpPool filtered to the era; all era opens on setup.startEra (random from ERAS when not given) and deals from Great People born on or after that era's first birth. Locations: 'all' picks 7 across eras, 'single' the chosen era.
notes: The lobby does not yet offer a start-era picker for all-era games; it is random.

title: Starting hand
docText: Each player is dealt 3 Great People (fewer, equal for everyone, in a small era), 2 Event cards and 8 Followers. The Great People are the earliest-born of the pool from the opening year, so the table starts as contemporaries.
codeBehaviour: openingDeal: handSize = min(STARTING_LINEAGES = 3, floor(upcoming / players)), dealt from the earliest-born, shuffled; eventHand = 2, followerHand = 8. No GP draw pile (gpDeck is empty on the timeline).
notes: Was 4 random Great People plus a draw pile before the timeline.

title: Locations on table
docText: All location cards revealed at start, columns = locations, rows = players.
codeBehaviour: 7 locations (NUM_LOCATIONS) chosen at random from data/locations.json; board rendered as a grid.
notes: Doc does not state the number of locations; code uses 7.

title: Follower deck
docText: Not specified.
codeBehaviour: 3 copies of each of the 32 follower templates = 96 cards, shuffled.
notes: Doc never states follower deck size.

title: Event deck
docText: 8 stats × 3 scenario types (24 scenario cards). Hazards are separate.
codeBehaviour: 24 scenario cards (one per stat × type). 8 hazard types in a separate deck used only for random placement.

title: City states at game start
docText: When history opens, each city can already be in a state of its own (same 30% roll as every new year).
codeBehaviour: initGame runs rollCityStates on the empty locations (unless setup.noHazards). Replaces the single random hazard placed at game start.

title: Legacies decide the game
docText: Completing the achievement that unlocks a Great Person's legacy gives the legacy. The most legacies at the end of history wins; there is no points race.
codeBehaviour: CLAIM_ACHIEVEMENT: public GP with achievementTicks ≥ legacy.unlock.wins and not already in player.legacies → legacy added (earnLegacy, which also still increments winningPoints for the timeless lessons), fills a free slot. leader() ranks by legacies.length.
notes: The board shows legacies (🏛) instead of points in timeline games.

title: End of history
docText: The game runs to 2030, or until no player has a Great Person now or to come; the most legacies wins (ties: seat order). No early win by points. Humans without lineages watch the computer play history out.
codeBehaviour: checkWinCondition (timeline): year ≥ TIMELINE_END_YEAR (2030) or no player with hasFuture → leader() by legacies. shouldFastForward also runs when no human has a Great Person left but a CPU does, so the CPU plays out to the end. Timeless games (Epic lessons) keep the 5-point win and "one player with GP".

title: One round is one year
docText: One round is one year in every era. Every game starts at a real year.
codeBehaviour: GameState.year advances by YEARS_PER_ROUND (1) in END_TURN when a new round starts (advanceYear). The header shows the year.

title: Birth and career start
docText: A Great Person enters the game in the year he/she was born and can be played from the career start: age 18, earlier for prodigies (careerAge on the card).
codeBehaviour: lifeStatus: unborn (year < born), youth (year < careerStartYear), active; careerStartYear = born + max(MIN_CAREER_AGE 4, careerAge ?? 18 − prodigy legacies).

title: Natural death
docText: A Great Person who outlives his/her death year dies wherever he/she is (hand, board or retirement). Living people live until the timeline ends.
codeBehaviour: advanceYear: deathYear(card, owner) < new year → removed from board/hand/retired, recordDeaths. deathYear = (died ?? 2030) + longevity legacies.

title: Successor born later
docText: When a Great Person dies (old age or killed in play) the player chooses a successor born later than the current year from the unclaimed Great People; the 3 nearest by birth are offered. The computer does the same.
codeBehaviour: pendingSuccessors queued by recordDeaths; successorOptions = unclaimed pool with born > year, nearest first, SUCCESSOR_CHOICES (3) + successor legacies; CHOOSE_SUCCESSOR for humans; resolveChoices picks the highest stat total for CPUs; no options → the lineage ends.
notes: Choices are presented in a modal on the board.

title: Retirement
docText: A player may retire a Great Person at any time on his/her turn. Retirement is not death: the successor waits for the real death year.
codeBehaviour: RETIRE_GP (current player, GP on board or in hand in youth/career) → PlayerState.retired. advanceYear kills retired GPs at their death year, which queues the successor.

title: Time skip
docText: When no human player has a Great Person in his/her career (and none owes a successor choice), time jumps ahead until one does; the computer plays out those years quickly.
codeBehaviour: settle → shouldFastForward → fastForward: advanceYear({fastForward}) per year (deaths, successions, states wear off, no new city states), CPU GPs on board win a legacy fight with FAST_FORWARD_CPU_WIN_CHANCE (5 %) per year and claim it; ends on a human career, a pending human choice, game end or 2030. Shows a time-skip summary.
notes: Also applies at game start, when every human Great Person is still too young.

title: A. Deploy a Great Person
docText: Once per turn, place a GP from hand to a location; choose public or private. Only a Great Person in his/her career can be brought on board.
codeBehaviour: DEPLOY_GP: once per turn (turnActions.deployedGP), isPublic chosen, card flagged justDeployed. On the timeline DEPLOY_GP is rejected unless lifeStatus is active (born + careerAge reached, not dead or retired).

title: B. Add a Follower
docText: Once per turn, add a follower to a location where you already have a GP.
codeBehaviour: ADD_FOLLOWER: once per turn, requires an allied GP at the location.
notes: Li Qingzhao / Michael Jackson traits that lift this limit are not implemented.

title: C. Move cards
docText: Any number of moves per turn, each card at most once.
codeBehaviour: MOVE_CARD tracked per instance in turnActions.movedCards; justDeployed cards cannot move.

title: D. Start an event
docText: A player may start an event only at a location where they have a Great Person that was not deployed this turn; most events are local.
codeBehaviour: START_EVENT places an event card from hand on a location, once per location per turn, and only if the player has a GP there with justDeployed === false (same presence check as END_SCENARIO). Global competitions use the same gate.
notes: In-game rules panel and selection hint say 'where you have a Great Person that was not deployed this turn'. The CPU AI never starts events, so it is unaffected.

title: E. Retrieve to hand
docText: Retrieve a GP or follower from the board to hand.
codeBehaviour: RETRIEVE_CARD returns GP id to gpHand / follower to followerHand; once per card per turn.

title: F. Claim a legacy
docText: Claim the legacy of a Great Person on board who completed the achievement: 1 winning point and the legacy. Once per legacy per player.
codeBehaviour: CLAIM_ACHIEVEMENT requires the card public, ticks ≥ legacy.unlock.wins and the legacy not yet earned; grants +1 point and the legacy. On the timeline no new GP is drawn; the timeless Epic lessons still draw one.
notes: The board button is labelled Claim Legacy.

title: G. Attack
docText: Attack any number of times per turn when both players have cards at the same location during a local event.
codeBehaviour: ATTACK allowed only when location.activeEvent.type === 'local_event'; no per-turn limit.
notes: Attacker's card is not required to be public (doc §7 says it must be).

title: H. End a local event
docText: A GP can end a scenario if it has the matching identity (e.g. Artist ends Art Critique).
codeBehaviour: END_SCENARIO: any non-just-deployed allied GP at the location can end any local event or survival, once per location per turn. Identity is not checked.

title: I. Toggle public/private
docText: Change a card's status; once per card per turn.
codeBehaviour: TOGGLE_VISIBILITY once per card per turn; justDeployed cards cannot toggle.

title: Just-deployed cards cannot act
docText: A GP or Follower that was just put on board cannot do C/D/E/F/I this turn.
codeBehaviour: justDeployed flag blocks move, retrieve, claim, visibility, end-scenario; cleared at END_TURN.
notes: Attack (G) is not blocked for just-deployed cards in either doc or code.

title: Phase order within a turn
docText: Deploy GP → Followers → Retrieve → Relocate → Visibility → Attack → Survival → Event → End scenario → New scenario → Achievement → Archive.
codeBehaviour: Free-form: any action can be taken in any order until END_TURN. Survival/hazard/global resolution happens only when a full round completes.

title: Reveal after attack
docText: After an attack, both players' cards at that location must all be public. Defender's cards auto-join and are revealed.
codeBehaviour: Only the two cards named in the ATTACK action are flipped public. Other allied/enemy cards at the location keep their status.

title: Private cards are hidden
docText: Face-down cards cannot be identified by other players.
codeBehaviour: CompactCard renders the card back for private cards of other players. State still contains the card id (client-side game).
notes: Hot-seat PvP: any player at the screen can inspect state via devtools.

title: Scenario names per stat
docText: politics: Coup/Terrorist Attack/International Conference; strength: Battlefield/Riot/Olympics; culture: Art Critique/Censorship/Roadshow; wealth: Business War/Depression/Auction; technique: Tech Race/Sanctions/World Fair; intelligence: Argument/Puzzle/Expedition; belief: Miracle/Inquisition/Pilgrimage; reputation: Lawsuit/Scandal/Celebration.
codeBehaviour: EVENT_NAMES matches the doc exactly.

title: Totals compared
docText: Compare the total of the stat over all GP and Followers of each player at the location (follower bonus included). Stronger side may attack.
codeBehaviour: computeLocationTotal = Σ GP base stat + implemented trait bonus + location bonus per GP, + follower bonus for followers whose stat matches.
notes: Doc has no notion of location bonus or trait numbers; engine adds both.

title: Winner chooses kill or retrieve
docText: Winner (sometimes the defender) chooses: kill → discard pile; otherwise loser is force-retrieved to hand. Draw → nothing.
codeBehaviour: Attacker chooses kill:boolean before attacking. The flag is applied to whichever side loses, so an attacker who loses is killed by its own choice. Draw → nothing. Only the single targeted card is removed, not the whole losing side.

title: Attacker must be public
docText: To attack, the GP must be public; public allied GP/Followers auto-join; defender's cards all revealed.
codeBehaviour: Not enforced: a private GP can attack. All allied cards (public or private) are summed.

title: Follower bonus
docText: 'Any follower bonus' is added to the GP total.
codeBehaviour: Follower adds its bonus (2) if its stat matches the scenario stat; 4 (FOLLOWER_IDENTITY_MATCH_BONUS) instead if an allied GP at the location has the follower's identity.
notes: Identity-match bonus (+4, raised from +3 by designer instruction) exists only in code; docs/fight.md does not state it.

title: Location bonus
docText: Not in fight.md. location_cards.json carries per-stat bonuses and a trait text per location.
codeBehaviour: Each GP at the location gains the location's bonus for the contested stat in conflicts only (not survival/hazard/global). Location trait texts are never executed.

title: Local survival threshold
docText: Any player at this location whose total for the stat (GP + followers) is below 10 is killed and discarded.
codeBehaviour: Threshold is 5: a player survives when total ≥ 5. Resolved at the start of each new round while the event stays active. Active survival-context legacies add to each side; Great People lost to a survival die (successor on the timeline).
notes: iOS/Android rules dialogs say 10. Card stats range 1–12, so a single GP survives at 5 only with a decent stat.

title: Survival persists
docText: The scenario keeps working until replaced by another event or ended by a GP.
codeBehaviour: eventRoundsLeft = 99 for local events/survival; replaced by START_EVENT or cleared by END_SCENARIO.

title: Special survival (hazard)
docText: Flood/Blizzard/Storm/Earthquake/Fire/Tsunami/Pandemic/Drought. Any player with total points (all stats, GP + followers) below 100 is killed. Random, lasts 1 round, placed where the drawer has most cards.
codeBehaviour: Per player: sum each of the 8 stats across their cards at the location; if the MINIMUM stat total < 5 they are discarded. 20% chance per new round, placed on the location with the most cards. Lasts 1 round. Hazard type has no effect. Active survival-context legacies add to the minimum; a hazard-shield legacy makes the player immune. Great People lost die (successor on the timeline). The old 20 % random hazard per round is replaced by city states.
notes: iOS/Android rules text says 'total stats below 100'. Three different rules exist.

title: Global competition
docText: All players involved; lasts 1 round; highest total of the stat over all PUBLIC cards on the board wins 2 events, 4 followers or 1 GP.
codeBehaviour: Sums base stat of public GP only (followers, traits and location bonuses ignored). Winner picks reward: 2 events / 4 followers / 1 GP. Competition-context legacies add to the player's total. On the timeline the Great Person reward founds a new lineage (a successor choice born after the current year).
notes: Followers excluded in code; doc says all cards.

title: Scenario replacement
docText: A scenario stays until replaced by another event or ended by a GP.
codeBehaviour: START_EVENT overwrites activeEvent at the location.

title: Cities fall into states by themselves
docText: Each year, a location with no scenario has a 30 % chance to enter a random local event (3 years), local survival (2 years) or natural hazard (1 year).
codeBehaviour: rollCityStates at every new year (advanceYear, or END_TURN in timeless games) and at initGame, unless setup.noHazards; CITY_STATE_CHANCE 0.3; randomCityState picks uniformly from 8 local events, 8 local survivals and 8 hazards; origin "city", durations CITY_STATE_YEARS. Not rolled during time skips.
notes: The Epic lessons set noHazards, so their boards stay as scripted.

title: Trait-driven scenario negation
docText: Gandhi negates all Conflict scenarios; Schumann shields from Survival for one round; Mani immune to Survival.
codeBehaviour: No scenario-level trait hooks exist.

title: Succession replaces archiving
docText: New Great People only arrive as successors: when a Great Person dies the player chooses one born later than the current year.
codeBehaviour: recordDeaths moves dead GPs to PlayerState.archive and queues pendingSuccessors; CHOOSE_SUCCESSOR picks from successorOptions; CPUs choose at once in settle/resolveChoices.
notes: There is still no voluntary "archive to draw" action; retirement (time-line) is the voluntary exit.

title: Global competition reward
docText: Winner of a global competition gets 2 event cards, 4 follower cards or 1 GP card.
codeBehaviour: GLOBAL_COMP_REWARD: 2 events or 4 followers from the decks; the GP reward is a new lineage on the timeline (pending successor) and a deck draw in timeless games.

title: Trait text is per-card data
docText: Each GP has a Characteristic (trait) that works while in the game.
codeBehaviour: traitBonusForGP implements numeric bonuses for 13 figures only; the other 67 traits have no effect. Several implemented bonuses differ from the card text (see Great People tab).

title: Trait idea doc vs cards.json
docText: great-people-trait-idea.md lists 28 draft traits/achievements.
codeBehaviour: cards.json is the shipped text; several entries were rewritten (e.g. Aspasia, Enkidu, Mani, Eisenstein, Peck) and some doc entries are blank (Musashi, Brahms, Titian, Clara, Montezuma, Mendel).
notes: Decide which document is canonical.

title: CPU visibility heuristics
docText: Not specified.
codeBehaviour: CPU keeps Belisarius, Musashi, Mao private and reveals Pericles/Aspasia-style cards; references traits that are not implemented (Musashi, Mao).

title: Achievement conditions (legacy unlock)
docText: Each card's achievement text says how its legacy is earned.
codeBehaviour: None of the textual conditions are evaluated. The engine checks legacy.unlock: a GP earns 1 tick when it attacks and kills an enemy GP in a local event of the unlock stat whose own value in that stat is ≥ 5; claim at unlock.wins ticks (1 for every card). Every card now has an unlock stat (previously 33 cards had none and were unreachable).
notes: Unlock stats come from the old ACHIEVEMENT_SPECS where one existed, otherwise the card's highest stat.

title: Legacy slots
docText: Claimed legacies are kept for the rest of the game; only those in the 2 legacy slots are in effect. One switch per turn.
codeBehaviour: PlayerState.legacies / activeLegacies; earnLegacy fills a free slot; SET_LEGACY once per turn (turnActions.legacyChanged), LEGACY_SLOTS = 2; CPUs fill free slots automatically.

title: Legacy effects
docText: Each legacy has a historically themed effect of one of 7 kinds: contest, follower, hazard shield, longevity, prodigy, successors, income.
codeBehaviour: legacyContest adds contest/follower bonuses in ATTACK (attack/defend), survivals and hazards (survival), global competitions (competition) and shows them as legacy rows in summaries; hasHazardShield; deathYear (longevity); careerStartYear (prodigy); successorOptions (successors); advanceYear (income).
notes: Effects are data (data/cards.json legacy.effect); editing them in Fight Studio needs no engine change.

title: Stat scale assumptions
docText: Al-Khwarizmi's achievement needs base stats 1–25; Brahms' trait uses a 25 threshold.
codeBehaviour: cards.json stats range 1–12 (demo_cards.json 1–24). Brahms implemented with a 13 threshold.
notes: Clarify the intended stat scale.

title: iOS/Android rules dialogs
docText: Not applicable (apps show a summary).
codeBehaviour: iOS BattleRulesView lists the timeline rules: end of history decided by legacies, careers, successors, retirement, time skips, legacy slots, survival and hazard below 5, 30 % city states. Android has no rules dialog: it opens the web Fight Arena.

title: Backend battle model
docText: great-people-card.md describes an older 10-card deck, simultaneous-play, 3-stat (Influence/Innovation/Legacy) round game, first to 5 rounds.
codeBehaviour: service/api/battle.py resolves a round by comparing one stat (round.active_stat) of two CardDefinition cards; first to 5. It does not model locations, followers, events or achievements. The web board game is purely client-side.
notes: Two different battle designs are documented; the board game only exists in the web client.
